mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is at or below 0.1%, accommodative monetary policy reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as observed in historical data.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE exceeding 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% indicate robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO > 0.5% MoM and HOUST > 0.5% MoM over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDP growth > 3% annualized and unemployment < 5.0%), RSAFS exceeding 400,000 signals sustained consumer spending momentum, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS > 400000 and the late-cycle expansion regime is active over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 900,000 units, robust consumer demand for housing and related sectors drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST > 900,000 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5% indicates aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous CPIAUCSL acceleration (MoM > 0.3%) and FEDFUNDS exceeding 0.5% signal inflationary monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 0.3% MoM and FEDFUNDS > 0.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), reduced consumer spending and corporate profit expectations cause negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% over a 5-year rolling window.
